history.dynasty: Hoysala (12th century origins); rebuilt 17th century in later Deccan style with contributions from Peshwas, Shindes and Holkars
history.period: Origins 1108-1152 CE; 1237 CE inscription; existing structure mainly 17th century or later
history.summary: The Shri Vitthal-Rukmini Mandir (Vithoba Temple) is the main centre of worship for Vithoba, a form of Vishnu/Krishna, and his consort Rakhumai, on the banks of the Chandrabhaga (Bhima) river at Pandharpur. It is one of the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams and the spiritual capital of the Warkari devotional tradition. Tradition holds that Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana (Bittideva) built it between 1108 and 1152 CE at the persuasion of the devotee Pundalik; a 1237 CE inscription of Hoysala king Vira Someshwara grants the temple a village for upkeep. The black-stone idol of Vitthala stands arms-akimbo on a brick, a pose legend attributes to Pundalik making Krishna wait while he served his parents. Parts date to the 12th-13th century but the present structure is mainly 17th-century Deccan style; the central idol survived an attack by Afzal Khan (destroyed a substitute idol), protected by the Badve priests. It is the only major temple where devotees may touch the deity's feet (Padarshana/Sparsh Darshan), and in 2014 it became the first in India to appoint women and people from lower castes as priests. Warkaris march here in Dindis for the Ekadashi yatras.

name: Shri Vitthal Rukmini Temple
town_description: Pandharpur is a holy pilgrimage town in Solapur district of Maharashtra, on the banks of the Chandrabhaga (Bhima) River, often called the spiritual capital of Maharashtra and the Southern Kashi. It is the beating heart of the Warkari tradition: saints like Namdev, Eknath and Tukaram sang here, and millions of Warkaris walk here in processions (Dindis) for Ashadhi and Kartiki Ekadashi. The town is compact, temple-dense, and lives off pilgrim traffic.

travel.airport: Solapur Airport, ~75-78 km (verify; limited connectivity). Pune Airport, ~200 km (most practical for flights).
travel.railway: Pandharpur Railway Station (on the Miraj-Kurduwadi-Latur line), ~2 km from the temple.
travel.road: ~73-75 km from Solapur, ~200-207 km from Pune (state transport buses and taxis); Mumbai ~360-500 km per conflicting sources (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: June-July (Ashadhi Ekadashi Yatra) and October-November (Kartiki Ekadashi); expect very heavy crowds on festival days.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00 AM - 11:00 PM daily (some sources say 11:45 PM close - CONFLICT (verify)). Kakad Aarti ~4:30 AM; darshan free (no paid darshan; online slot booking free). Mobile phones and photography strictly prohibited inside.
